newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook - Charts still bearish for tired gold.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook - Charts still bearish for tired gold.

text.p: Gold's failure last week to break above the key $330 resistance level has left it increasingly vulnerable to test downside support and eventually head towards new 12-year lows, chartists said on Monday.
A sharp drop on Wall Street last Friday gave the market a modicum of support amid investor concerns about a big stock market correction.

But the caution of investors, fears of producer selling and a general market malaise helped capped the rise, dealers said. On Monday prices were hovering around $326.00 an ounce, compared with $324.10/$324.60 at Friday's London close
"People aren't rushing in. They want to see whether the situtation with the stock market continues or was just a one-off," a dealer said.
Technically gold remained range-bound in a broad $320-$330 band, but its repeated inability to move beyond the $330 level suggested further weakness was forthcoming, analysts said.

"I don't see anything particularly positive in a broad sense at all. The downward cycle is still in force and one can still build a case for the market edging lower in the weeks ahead," said technical analyst Cliff Green of Trend Analysis.

On the downside, breaks below first support around $325 would target $318 and then $313.50-$314 would come under pressure once more, added Green, noting that there were no obvious technical patterns developing on gold charts.
Below those 12-year lows further acceleration to the downside would be potentially triggered.
On the upside, the $329-$330 area remained the top end of a reconsolidation phase which gold needed to hurdle to relieve immediate downward pressure and suggest an upward correction.
In that event, gold might target $336 or $340.
"But even that is not going to confirm a major reversal. All it would do is suggest a better correction -- a chance to sell at a higher level," Green said.
In other precious metals, silver was edging higher and consolidation in the $4.50-$4.60 level was expected while the market pondered its next move.
Technically silver has been following gold and was likely to continue taking cues from the yellow metal.
The platinum group metals remained tight, although Russian material trickling into the market had depressed palladium, which was encountering support at $210 an ounce.
